quotes.quote: "We held off on making any moves. I was nervous, and we ended up leaving in a panic without a plan." -- Bailey

"It felt odd leaving the neighborhood without one of our cars, but knowing it was safe elsewhere gave us peace of mind. We could focus on getting out without worrying about what we were leaving behind." -- Bailey
"We tried to leave one car parked safely, but when the fire got close, we just panicked and took both. It slowed us down in traffic, but thankfully we made it." -- Bailey

"Leaving one car felt strange, but with just the essentials, we moved quickly and avoided most of the traffic. Knowing we could focus on getting to safety rather than worrying about the extra car was a relief." -- Bailey
"We just couldn't leave one of the cars, so we took both. The streets were packed, and it was nerve-wracking, but thankfully, we were able to stay together." -- Bailey
"We decided to take both cars so each of us could bring what we needed. It slowed us down a bit in the evacuation, but we felt better having everything with us." -- Bailey
"It was hard to leave the kids, but the school was a safe place. I trusted the staff and focused on getting us ready at home. Knowing they were safe gave me one less thing to worry about." -- Gabe

"We planned to leave them at school, but I just couldn't. I rushed over, picked them up, and got caught in traffic on the way back. It was a tough decision, but I couldn't stand the thought of being separated." -- Gabe

"I didn't want to take any chances, so I went to get them as soon as I could. It took a bit longer with everyone on the road, but we made it back together, and it was worth the peace of mind." -- Gabe

"I thought about getting them, but we waited. The school kept them safe, and we were able to prepare the house and pack our things in the meantime. In the end, I'm glad we didn't risk getting stuck in traffic." -- Gabe
"We held off on making any moves. I was nervous, and we ended up leaving in a panic without a plan." -- Gabe
"Leaving early was tough, but knowing we had a head start on everyone else made it worth it. It wasn't easy to leave the house behind, but safety comes first." -- Sarah
"We thought we had more time. In the end, it was a close call, and it reminded us just how dangerous it is to live out here. Next time, we won't risk it." -- Sarah
"Investing in our home's defenses has been worth it. We know it's not foolproof, but at least we're giving our place a fighting chance if a fire comes close." -- Sarah
"It was too expensive to do upgrades and we thought everything would work out okay, but now we are devastated to have lost our house." -- Sarah
"We decided to wait and see but things got out of hand so quickly. We are relieved that emergency responders were available to help us, but we know next time we might not be so lucky." -- Sarah
"Leaving early felt strange, but it gave me time to travel safely and avoid the rush. I’m glad I didn’t wait." -- June
"I waited too long, and leaving became stressful. Thankfully, my neighbors helped, but I’ve learned my lesson about waiting." -- June
"I reached out to my neighbors, and we made a plan. Knowing they had my back made all the difference during the evacuation." -- June
"I thought I could manage on my own, but it was harder than I expected. Next time, I’ll accept the help." -- June
"We held off on making any moves. I was nervous, and we ended up leaving in a panic without a plan." -- June
"We held off on making any moves. I was nervous, and we ended up leaving in a panic without a plan." -- Genaro
"Having everything ready—crates, food, and a plan—made evacuating so much easier. The pets stayed calm, and we didn’t have to scramble." -- Genaro
"We left in a rush, and it was total chaos trying to manage the pets without supplies. I won’t make that mistake again." -- Genaro
"Leaving early felt a little overcautious, but it was worth it. No stress, no traffic, and the pets were safe the whole time." -- Genaro
"We stayed longer than we should have, and getting out with the pets was way harder than expected. Next time, we’re leaving earlier." -- Genaro
